meshy_task.text_style_prompt: Burrowback, a stylised badger creature. Body fur is dark chocolate brown with a slight bark texture; face has a bold cream-white stripe down the middle with black-brown eye bands and cream cheeks; black nose. The back carries distinct cool grey stone plates with crisp darker grey edges and small olive-moss patches between them, clearly separated from the brown fur. Pale ivory claws, dark brown paws, brown bushy tail. Matte hand-painted stylised look, clean colour blocks, no noise, no speckle. No red, no pink, no rust, no maroon, no oxblood anywhere.

palette.red_metric: texels with HSV hue <24 or >320 deg, saturation >0.25, value >0.12 (the retex worker clamp rule), over the whole 2048 atlas

transfer.atlas_identity: candidate Image_0 is byte-identical to the recovered model texture (sha256 609cc5b074335e5f2436f5fe3bd7775bdc7fd4c52cf8346f28a31d12139a1897)

uv_check.method: candidate triangle centroids (decimated mesh) projected to the nearest retexture triangle after bbox normalisation and best of 8 yaw/mirror alignments; interpolated UV compared to centroid UV

transfer.uv_check_summary: Decimated candidate UVs sample the retexture atlas consistently: median 0.27 texel error at triangle centroids, 91.6% within 1 texel, 98.8% within 4 texels. The retex worker found retexture (position, UV) pairs match the recovered model 99.99-100% (welds only), and the candidate atlas is byte-identical to the recovered texture, so the maps occupy the exact atlas space the candidate already samples. The remaining centroids are ordinary-sized triangles (median longest UV edge 14.82 texels vs 17.23 for inliers, so not seam-straddling) whose nearest retexture surface after bbox normalisation lies on another UV island (thin or near-coincident sheets); they still sample the same atlas texels the candidate samples with its original Image_0, because the UVs themselves are unchanged.
transfer.maps: base colour, metallic-roughness (packed; metallicFactor/roughnessFactor 1.0 from the Meshy material) and normal from the retexture GLB embedded images
